ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct pale, yellowish-white mid-dorsal stripe and granular skin. It features a pointed snout and prominent, protruding eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Periyar Night Frog is best distinguished by its unique, extremely elongated third finger, which is significantly longer than those of other *Nyctibatrachus* species.
ai.habitat: The Periyar Night Frog inhabits mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at altitudes between 900 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Periyar Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along stream banks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus periyar* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of 20–30 large, unpigmented eggs in rock crevices or vegetation near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Periyar Night Frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, specifically occurring in the Periyar Tiger Reserve of Kerala at elevations above 900 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Periyar Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" chirps, typically heard from vegetation near fast-flowing streams in its rainforest habitat.
